items.stem: Arjun writes a program for Nova Telecom that adds 0.1 to a REAL variable Total, starting from 0, 100 times, then tests IF Total = 10 THEN OUTPUT "Correct". items.answer: (a) 0.1 cannot be stored exactly in binary, so each addition adds a small rounding error; after 100 additions Total is not exactly 10 (b) IF ABS(Total − 10) < 0.0001 THEN ... (c) more mantissa bits give greater precision so the error is smaller, but it is not removed
items.markingKey: (a) 0.1 not exact [1]; rounding errors accumulate [1] (b) compare with a tolerance [2] (c) smaller error but still present [2]

items.stem: What does the mantissa hold in floating-point representation?
options: The position of the binary point
The number of bits used
The significant digits of the number
Only the sign of the number
items.answer: The significant digits of the number
items.markingKey: Mantissa: the precision; exponent: the range/scale.

items.stem: A floating-point number has an 8-bit two's complement mantissa 10110100 and a 4-bit two's complement exponent 0000. Tomás calculates its denary value as 1.40625. Explain the error and give the correct value.
items.answer: Tomás treated the mantissa as unsigned; its first bit has place value −1, so the mantissa is negative. Correct value: -0.59375 × 2^0 = -0.59375.
items.markingKey: 1 mark error identified; 1 mark correct mantissa/exponent; 1 mark correct value [3]

items.stem: A floating-point number has an 8-bit two's complement mantissa 01000001 and a 4-bit two's complement exponent 1111. Tariq calculates its denary value as 16640. Explain the error and give the correct value.
items.answer: Tariq treated the exponent 1111 as unsigned (15); in two's complement it is -1. Correct value: 0.5078125 × 2^-1 = 0.25390625.
items.markingKey: 1 mark error identified; 1 mark correct mantissa/exponent; 1 mark correct value [3]

items.stem: Convert the denary number 13.5 into a normalised floating-point number with an 8-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent, both in two's complement.
items.answer: Mantissa 01101100, exponent 0100
items.markingKey: 13.5 in binary, normalised so the mantissa starts 01 (1); mantissa 01101100 (1); exponent 0100 (= 4) (1) [3]

items.stem: A floating-point number uses an 8-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent, both in two's complement. Calculate the denary value of mantissa 01010110, exponent 1110.
items.markingKey: Exponent 1110 = -2 (1); move the binary point 2 places left (mantissa 0.671875 × 2^-2) (1); value 0.16796875 (1) [3]

items.stem: Convert the denary number 113 into a normalised floating-point number with an 8-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent, both in two's complement.
items.answer: Mantissa 01110001, exponent 0111
items.markingKey: 113 in binary, normalised so the mantissa starts 01 (1); mantissa 01110001 (1); exponent 0111 (= 7) (1) [3]

items.stem: Two floating-point numbers use an 8-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent in two's complement. P: mantissa 01101001, exponent 1101. Q: mantissa 10001010, exponent 0010. (a) Calculate the denary value of P. (b) Calculate the denary value of Q. (c) Calculate P + Q in denary. (d) State, with a reason, whether both numbers are normalised.
items.answer: (a) 0.1025390625 (b) -3.6875 (c) -3.5849609375 (d) yes: P starts 01 (positive) and Q starts 10 (negative)
items.markingKey: (a) exponent -3; 0.1025390625 [2] (b) exponent 2; -3.6875 [2] (c) -3.5849609375 [1] (d) first two mantissa bits differ in both [1]

items.stem: Two floating-point numbers use an 8-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent in two's complement. P: mantissa 01001011, exponent 1111. Q: mantissa 10111000, exponent 0010. (a) Calculate the denary value of P. (b) Calculate the denary value of Q. (c) Calculate P + Q in denary. (d) State, with a reason, whether both numbers are normalised.
items.answer: (a) 0.29296875 (b) -2.25 (c) -1.95703125 (d) yes: P starts 01 (positive) and Q starts 10 (negative)
items.markingKey: (a) exponent -1; 0.29296875 [2] (b) exponent 2; -2.25 [2] (c) -1.95703125 [1] (d) first two mantissa bits differ in both [1]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) A negative normalised floating-point mantissa always starts with which two bits? (b) A positive normalised floating-point mantissa always starts with which two bits?
items.markingKey: (a) The first two bits of a normalised mantissa are different. (b) Positive normalised: 0 then 1; negative normalised: 1 then 0.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Each number has only one normalised representation. Reason (R): A normalised positive mantissa starts with 00. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "A normalised positive mantissa starts with 00." is incorrect.

items.stem: The floating-point number with mantissa 00000011 and exponent 0000 (8-bit and 4-bit two's complement) is not normalised. Explain how you can tell, and normalise it.
items.answer: A normalised mantissa must start 01 (positive) or 10 (negative); this one starts 00. Shift the mantissa left 5 place(s) and subtract 5 from the exponent: mantissa 01100000, exponent 1011 (value unchanged: 0.0234375).
items.markingKey: 1 mark reason; 1 mark mantissa; 1 mark exponent [3]

items.stem: The floating-point number with mantissa 00111010 and exponent 1110 (8-bit mantissa, 4-bit exponent, two's complement) is not normalised. Normalise it, giving the new mantissa and exponent.
items.answer: Mantissa 01110100, exponent 1101
items.markingKey: Shift the mantissa 1 place left so the first two bits differ: 01110100 (1); exponent -2 − 1 = -3 = 1101 (1) [2]

items.stem: The floating-point number with mantissa 11100011 and exponent 0011 (8-bit mantissa, 4-bit exponent, two's complement) is not normalised. Normalise it, giving the new mantissa and exponent.
items.answer: Mantissa 10001100, exponent 0001
items.markingKey: Shift the mantissa 2 places left so the first two bits differ: 10001100 (1); exponent 3 − 2 = 1 = 0001 (1) [2]

items.stem: A scientific instrument at Nova Telecom stores readings as 8-bit mantissa, 4-bit exponent floating-point numbers. (a) Convert mantissa 10011110, exponent 0111 to denary. (b) Explain why the readings should be stored in normalised form. (c) State how you can tell whether a negative mantissa is normalised.
items.answer: (a) -98 (b) Maximum precision for the bits available and a unique representation of each value. (c) Its first two bits are 10.
items.markingKey: (a) exponent 7; value -98 [2] (b) 1 mark each [2] (c) 1 mark [1]

items.stem: Why can 0.1 not be stored exactly in binary floating-point?
options: Its binary form is a recurring fraction that would need infinitely many bits
It needs a negative exponent
It is too large
It is negative
items.answer: Its binary form is a recurring fraction that would need infinitely many bits
items.markingKey: 0.1 = 0.000110011... in binary, so it is rounded.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Floating-point numbers never have rounding errors. Reason (R): More significant bits can be stored, so the number can be represented more accurately. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is false but R is true
items.markingKey: A is false: "Floating-point numbers never have rounding errors." is incorrect; R is a true statement.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Underflow can occur when two very small numbers are multiplied. Reason (R): Its binary representation is a recurring fraction. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: A floating-point system uses a 12-bit mantissa and a 4-bit exponent, both in two's complement. Give the mantissa and exponent of the most negative value that can be represented, and its denary value.
items.answer: Mantissa 100000000000, exponent 0111; -128
